source_refs.note: Book p. 252: 8.5.4 Cryptography, Example 4 Key Parameter (shown as Example 11): x^5 - 10x + 5 = 0 by Regula-Falsi on [1, 2], iteration table, x = 1.62.

blocks.text: Cryptographic algorithms sometimes involve high-degree nonlinear equations to generate secure keys or pseudo-random numbers.

blocks.title: Numbering note (ours)
blocks.text: The book prints this example as 'Example 4' (the second Example 4 in this unit); we show it as Example 11 (see the note in 8.5.1).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: A degree-five polynomial has no general formula for its roots, so a numerical method is the natural tool. The question asks for 'a real value': the book chooses the root in \([1, 2]\).

blocks.title: Example 11
blocks.problem:
Key Parameter. In a cryptosystem, a key parameter \(x\) satisfies the equation \(x^{5} - 10x + 5 = 0\). Find a real value of \(x\) correct to two decimal places using the Regula-Falsi method.
Note: \(x\) represents a component of the encryption key; its approximate value is crucial for secure key generation.
steps:
Given: \(x^{5} - 10x + 5 = 0\).
To find: a real root \(x\), correct to two decimal places.
Method: Regula-Falsi on an interval of sign change. Since \(b\) will stay fixed at 2 with \(f(2) = 17\), each step only needs the new \(a\) and \(f(a)\).

Define function
\[f(x) = x^{5} - 10x + 5\]
Why: Regula-Falsi finds a root of \(f(x) = 0\).

Select interval
\[f(1) = 1 - 10 + 5 = -4 < 0\]
\[f(2) = 32 - 20 + 5 = 17 > 0\]
Why: opposite signs, so a root lies in \([1, 2]\).

Continuity
Note that \(f(c) = \lim_{x \to c} (x^{5} - 10x + 5)\) for every \(c \in [1, 2]\).
\(f\) is continuous on the interval of sign change \([1, 2]\).
Why: f is a polynomial; continuity makes the Location of Root Theorem and the method valid.

Iteration 3: a = 1.3603, b = 2
\[x_c = \dfrac{1.3603(17) + 2(3.9453)}{17 + 3.9453}\]
\[= \dfrac{31.0157}{20.9453} = 1.4808\]
\[f(1.4808) = -2.6880\]
Why: the iterations continue in the same way; the book lists all of them in the Regula-Falsi Iteration Table below.

Checking
\(|f(1.6216)| = 0.0031 < 0.01\)
Why: \(f\) is practically zero at 1.6216 (also below 0.005, the tolerance of 8.3.1), so \(x \approx 1.62\).

Check:
Sign test (ours): \(f(1.615) \approx -0.1634 < 0\) and \(f(1.625) \approx 0.0810 > 0\), so the root lies in \(]1.615, 1.625[\) and rounds to 1.62.
The exact root in \([1, 2]\) is \(x = 1.6217\ldots\)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text:
1. Row 4: from \(a = 1.4808\) (\(f(a) = -2.6880\)) and \(b = 2\) (\(f(b) = 17\)) the formula gives \(x_c = \frac{30.5496}{19.6880} = 1.5517\) with \(f(1.5517) = -1.5212\); the book prints 1.5523. Rows 5-9 are then worked correctly from that printed value, so the slip only changes the numbers a little.
2. Row 10 is impossible: Regula-Falsi on \([1.6203, 2]\) gives \(x_c = \frac{27.6151}{17.0350} = 1.6211\) with \(f(1.6211) = -0.0154\), not 1.6581 with \(f = +0.9520\). Since \(f > 0\) at 1.6581 the printed point lies past the root; a secant through \((1.6203, -0.0350)\) and \((2, 17)\) cannot cut the axis there. Row 11's interval \([1.6203, 1.6581]\) is wrong for the same reason.
3. Worked correctly (table below) the iterations continue 1.6211, 1.6214, 1.6216, and stop at \(|f(1.6216)| = 0.0031\). The book's final answer \(x \approx 1.62\) is correct (exact root 1.6217...).

blocks.caption: Book correction (ours): the Regula-Falsi table worked correctly (4 decimal places)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Why is Regula-Falsi slow here (11-12 iterations)? On \([1, 2]\) the curve bends upwards (\(f''(x) = 20x^{3} > 0\)), so every secant line lies above the curve and cuts the axis to the LEFT of the root. Hence \(b = 2\) never moves, and because \(f(2) = 17\) is huge compared with \(f(a)\), each step creeps forward only a little.
With \(b\) fixed the formula simplifies to \(x_c = \frac{17a - 2f(a)}{17 - f(a)}\), which makes the table quicker to fill.
The equation has two more real roots: \(f(0) = 5 > 0\) and \(f(1) = -4 < 0\) give one in \([0, 1]\) (\(x \approx 0.50\)), and there is one near \(-1.89\). The question only asks for 'a real value'.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: When one end stays fixed, write \(f(b)\) once and reuse it; check each new \(x_c\) lies between the current \(a\) and \(b\). A value outside the interval (like the printed 1.6581 with \(f > 0\)) is a sure sign of an arithmetic slip.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
Key model: \(x^{5} - 10x + 5 = 0\), \(f(1) = -4\), \(f(2) = 17\): root in \([1, 2]\).
Regula-Falsi with \(b = 2\) fixed; every \(f(x_c) < 0\) replaces \(a\).
Stop at \(|f(1.6216)| = 0.0031\): \(x \approx 1.62\).
Every new point must stay inside the current interval.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
Writing \(-2(-4)\) as \(-8\) in the first iteration: it is \(+8\), giving \(25/21\).
Replacing b when f(x_c) is negative: the end with the same sign as f(x_c) (here a) is replaced.
Stopping at |f| = 0.0080 when the 8.3.1 tolerance for two places is 0.005.
